clue.text: Cultivated area of study after review of old material

indicators.note: after puts the study piece behind the reversed material in the answer
a review looks back over something, so the word for old material is read backwards

parts.note: rag is a scrap of old cloth
a den is a private room for work or study

explanation.surface: A field of study taken up after looking back over some dusty old material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cultivated area' is the definition, not a field of study; 'study' here is a room.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot where plants are grown and tended is the plainest example of a cultivated area.

clue.text: Flashy guy has ad regularly inserted

indicators.note: has here means the man's word takes the advert letters into itself around its middle letter

parts.note: guy is written as it stands; its middle letter U is the one the A and D of ad go either side of

indicators.note: the two letters of the advert word go in at regular intervals, one before and one after the middle letter of the man's word

parts.note: guy's middle letter U is the one the A and D of ad go either side of

explanation.surface: A showy fellow has had an advertisement placed in the middle of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly inserted' means the A and D go in alternately between the letters of GUY, at every other position.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something showy and tastelessly bright, a straightforward synonym pair.

clue.text: During short dance knees get bad again

indicators.note: during says one piece sits within the time, and so within the letters, of the other
short says the dance word loses its final letter

parts.note: a reel is a lively Scottish dance
with knees bent while seated, the tops of the thighs form one's lap, so knees stand for laps

explanation.surface: Someone's knees get worse again in the middle of a brief dance.
explanation.walkthrough: A reel is a lively Scottish dance; the lap is formed by the thighs above bent knees.
explanation.definitionFit: To relapse is to fall back into illness after seeming to recover, i.e. to worsen once more.

clue.text: Old timer banks on open and friendly person

indicators.note: in a down clue on puts the first pieces above the open word

parts.note: ex means former, as in an ex-partner

indicators.note: banks are the edges of a river, so the outer letters of timer are taken

parts.note: overt means done openly, not hidden

explanation.surface: An old timekeeper relies on someone who is open and sociable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banks' gives the outer letters T and R of 'timer'.
explanation.definitionFit: An outgoing, sociable person who seeks company is the classic opposite of an introvert.

clue.text: Recent shift in focus

indicators.note: a shift is a change of position, so the letters of recent move around

explanation.surface: There has lately been a change in what people are concentrating on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shift' rearranges RECENT; 'shift in focus' reads as a stock phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The focus of something is its central point of attention, a synonym in the noun sense.

clue.text: The King of the Spanish taking victory over islands

parts.note: el is the Spanish for the
V is the standard abbreviation for victory, as in V-sign
IS is a map abbreviation for islands

explanation.surface: A Spanish monarch wins and takes possession of some islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The King' looks like part of a Spanish royal title, but it is Presley's nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: Presley was widely nicknamed the King of Rock and Roll.

clue.text: Reprimand for bad mark earlier

indicators.note: earlier puts the mark ahead of the bad word in the answer

parts.note: a tick is a check mark on a list
food that is off has gone bad

explanation.surface: A telling-off given because of an earlier poor grade.
explanation.walkthrough: TICK OFF is British slang for scold.
explanation.definitionFit: To scold someone sharply is to tick them off in informal British usage.

clue.text: Finish first ultra marathon heartened by new stamina

parts.note: end means finish

indicators.note: first takes just the opening letter of the following word
heartened by says the race word gets something in its heart

parts.note: a marathon is a long running race

explanation.surface: Completing the first ultramarathon, cheered on by fresh stamina.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' gives U from 'ultra'; 'heartened by' puts N inside RACE for RANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Staying power to keep going over a long effort is what both words describe.

clue.text: Property in harbour's bright inside

indicators.note: inside puts the bright word within the harbour word

parts.note: a quay is a landing place in a harbour
lit means lit up, bright

explanation.surface: A piece of real estate by the harbour has a bright interior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Property' suggests a building, but it means a characteristic.
explanation.definitionFit: A property in the sense of an attribute or characteristic of something is one of its qualities.

clue.text: A very old colon's beginning to have trouble with fruit

indicators.note: to have joins the trouble word on at the end
beginning takes the first letter of the colon word

parts.note: ado means fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: A very old person's bowel trouble is put down to eating fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning' gives C from 'colon'.
explanation.definitionFit: The pear-shaped green produce from a tropical tree is botanically a berry, so a fruit.

clue.text: Retaliate, greeting silly attack initially by blocking

parts.note: hi is a greeting

indicators.note: blocking says that letter stands in the middle of the jumbled attack letters
silly says the letters of attack are jumbled
initially takes the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Respond in kind, after a greeting turns into a foolish attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silly' turns ATTACK into TACKAT; 'initially' gives B from 'by'; 'blocking' places it inside for TBACKAT.
explanation.definitionFit: To retaliate is to strike back at whoever struck first; the phrasal verb is the idiom.

clue.text: Young woman's going back over fakes of classical works

indicators.note: over says the reversed title is spread over the young letter, enclosing it
going back says the title is read in reverse

parts.note: Ms is the title for a woman
phonies are frauds or fakes

explanation.surface: A young woman goes back over forged pieces of classical music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going back' turns MS to SM; 'over' wraps it round Y for SYM.
explanation.definitionFit: Large orchestral compositions in several movements are among the best-known works of classical music.

clue.text: Vegetable's fine almost raw

parts.note: OK means fine, all right

indicators.note: almost drops the last letter of raw

explanation.surface: A vegetable that is fine to eat nearly uncooked.
explanation.definitionFit: The green pods also called ladies' fingers are a vegetable used in gumbo.

clue.text: First lady is in retreat for strain

indicators.note: in retreat means going backwards, so the word is is reversed

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in the Bible

explanation.surface: The President's wife withdraws because of stress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First lady' suggests a president's wife; it is Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: To strain is to pass something through a mesh utensil, which this kitchen tool does.

clue.text: Putting up statue in Piccadilly location's a sensitive issue

indicators.note: in a down clue putting up means the letters are read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: Eros is the winged figure on the fountain at Piccadilly Circus in London
a point is a location, as in a meeting point

explanation.surface: Erecting a statue at a spot in Piccadilly is a touchy subject.
explanation.walkthrough: The statue in Piccadilly Circus, London, is popularly called Eros; 'Putting up' turns it to SORE.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic that upsets or irritates someone when raised is an idiomatic touchy subject.

clue.text: Meeting gets cheese and fruit around noon

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese

indicators.note: around says the fruit word goes round the noon letter

parts.note: a fig is a fruit

explanation.surface: A meeting with a lunchtime spread of cheese and fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A meeting where people are given information or instructions before a task is this kind of session.

clue.text: Ruinous tax return has Jack heading off raging

indicators.note: return here means the tax letters are turned back

parts.note: NI is National Insurance, a UK payroll tax
J is the abbreviation for jack in a pack of cards

indicators.note: heading off removes the first letter of the raging word

parts.note: furious means raging

explanation.surface: A crippling tax return has someone named Jack storming off in fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tax return' reads as a form; NI is National Insurance, a UK tax.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something that causes great harm or damage, near synonyms.

clue.text: Creative trait is developed by college

indicators.note: by puts the college letter beside, at the end
developed means worked into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An inventive streak is cultivated by attending college.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing imagination and skill in making things is the meaning of both words.

clue.text: Vulgar new gin joint's briefly set up

indicators.note: new says the letters of gin are formed anew in another order
in a down clue set up means the letters go upward, read backwards
briefly cuts the last letter from the joint word

parts.note: the elbow is a joint of the arm

explanation.surface: A crude new gin bar is quickly opened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns GIN into IGN; 'briefly' cuts ELBOW to ELBO and 'set up' reverses it to OBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean base or low in character, lacking nobility.

clue.text: Extract right idiot from Jurassic ride at last

indicators.note: from says the right and idiot letters are taken away from Jurassic

parts.note: an ass is a fool

indicators.note: at last takes the final letter of ride

explanation.surface: Pull a foolish person off the Jurassic Park ride at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking RASS out of JURASSIC leaves JUIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid pressed out of fruit is an extract of it; noun sense.

clue.text: List some climbing buddies I met individually

indicators.note: climbing says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Write down a few of the friends one has met, one by one.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'climbing' reads the run upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To list things is to set them out one by one, item by item, as a verb.

clue.text: Bites back politically biased comment

indicators.note: back says the bites word is read in reverse

parts.note: nips are small bites

explanation.surface: A partisan remark comes back to bite someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Spin is the slanted presentation of facts by press officers to favour a party.

clue.text: Sails through following main coastal winds

indicators.note: following puts the sails-through word after the main word

parts.note: the main is an old word for the open sea
breezes means does something easily, sails through it

explanation.surface: A boat glides easily ahead on the open ocean with the shore winds behind it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'main' is the poetic word for the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Light winds blowing in off the ocean onto the shore are typical coastal winds.

clue.text: Genuine soldiers disappeared after that time

indicators.note: disappeared says the soldiers are removed from the genuine word

parts.note: sincere means genuine
RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of British soldiers

explanation.surface: Real troops went missing after that.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adverb the word means from then on, after a past time.

clue.text: Hiding inside blasted tree's good for bird

indicators.note: hiding inside says the good letter is tucked within the other letters
blasted means wrecked, so the letters of tree are scrambled

explanation.surface: A bird finds a good hiding place inside a lightning-blasted tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blasted' turns TREE into ERET; G goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A white heron of marshes and estuaries is a wading bird.

clue.text: Travelling bans did break up the group

indicators.note: travelling means moving about, so the letters rearrange

explanation.surface: Restrictions on touring forced the band to split.
explanation.definitionFit: To dissolve an organisation or team so it no longer exists is to break it up.

clue.text: Tights, hard to get with very large denier, half gone by end of day

indicators.note: by places the day letter next to the rest at the end

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
OS is the abbreviation for outsize, very large in clothing

indicators.note: half gone says the first half of denier is dropped
end of takes the final letter of day

explanation.surface: Getting tights in a very heavy denier is tricky, half of them gone by close of business.
explanation.walkthrough: Denier measures the thickness of hosiery yarn.
explanation.definitionFit: Stockings, tights and socks are all sold as this class of knitted legwear.

clue.text: Note fencing equipment in tent

parts.note: te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
an epee is a fencing sword

explanation.surface: A reminder that fencing kit is kept in the tent.
explanation.definitionFit: A conical tent of skins on poles used by Plains peoples of North America is a type of tent.

clue.text: Look at technical details coming in

indicators.note: coming in says the details go inside the word at

parts.note: spec is short for specification, technical details

explanation.surface: Examine the specifications as they arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look at' reads as a phrase, but 'Look' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's look or appearance is their aspect; noun sense.
